(CNN) -- Barcelona delivered a dazzling display of attacking football, routing arch-rivals Real Madrid 6-2 at the Bernabeu to all but secure the Primera Liga title. Two goals apiece from Lionel Messi and Thierry Henry, complemented by strikes from defenders Carles Puyol and Gerard Pique, inflicted a humiliating defeat on a Real side that had entered "El Clasico" with renewed hope of retaining the Spanish crown.

A combination of inspired attacking play and calamitous defending undermined Juande Ramos' men, who had taken an early lead when Gonzalo Higuain headed home after 14 minutes. Henry swiftly equalized with a clinical finish after Messi's incisive through ball split the offside trap, before an unmarked Puyol headed Barcelona in front in the 20th minute from a Xavi free-kick. Messi then glided through the Real defense—following a clever interception by Xavi—to put his side 3-1 ahead before halftime.

Sergio Ramos briefly rekindled Madrid's hopes in the 56th minute, heading home from an Arjen Robben free-kick, but any prospect of a comeback was swiftly extinguished. Henry latched onto a sublime through ball from Xavi to restore the three-goal cushion, before Messi added a fifth with an audacious finish that left Iker Casillas rooted to the spot—his 23rd league goal of the season. The rout was completed when Samuel Eto'o surged down the right flank and crossed for Pique, who deftly turned to beat Casillas for the sixth goal—his first-ever strike in La Liga.

The result marked Barcelona's 100th league goal of the campaign, extending their remarkable tally to 27 wins from 34 matches. Real Madrid supporters streamed toward the exits well before the final whistle, struggling to process the heaviest defeat ever suffered by their club at the Santiago Bernabeu. With just four games remaining, Real now trail Barcelona by seven points, while a supremely confident Barcelona side turns its attention to the second leg of their Champions League semifinal against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, following a goalless first leg.

Elsewhere, Sevilla took a significant step toward Champions League qualification with a 2-0 victory over rivals Villarreal in Saturday's late match. Goals from Luis Fabiano and Freddy Kanoute lifted third-placed Sevilla four points clear of Valencia and five ahead of Villarreal.
